memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: In cases of defiling skin diseases, be very careful to do exactly as the Levitical priests instruct you. You must follow carefully what I have commanded them. Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam along the way after you came out of Egypt. - Deut 24:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God instructs His people to carefully follow the priests' guidance regarding skin diseases, and then adds a pointed reminder, "Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam." Miriam, Moses' sister, had spoken against Moses and was struck with a skin disease for a time as a consequence (Num 12). God calls His people to remember that event and to take His instructions seriously.

The point is not fear for fear's sake, but a healthy reverence that heeds God's warnings. Miriam's experience was a real lesson, and God did not want it forgotten. His commands were given for the good of His people, and ignoring them brought harm. Remembering past lessons helps us walk more faithfully in the present.

We can draw a wise principle from this, that we do well to remember the lessons God has taught us, whether through Scripture or through our own experiences. God's warnings are acts of love, meant to keep us from harm. The New Testament tells us that the accounts of the Old Testament were written down as examples and warnings for us, to help us learn and not repeat the same mistakes (1 Cor 10:11). Rather than dismissing correction or forgetting hard lessons, we grow when we take them to heart. What lessons has God taught you that you need to keep remembering, so that you walk more wisely today?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What lessons has God taught you that you tend to forget?
2. How do you respond to God's warnings and correction?
3. How can remembering the past help you walk wisely now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me take Your warnings to heart and remember the lessons You have taught me. Let me walk wisely, learning from the past. Amen.
